title: The Contact of Marseille's old port
premise: Xanthe Reyes, a private security contractor who has spent seven years erasing her past, is guarding a Marseille shipping magnate when a routine voiceprint scan unlocks a server in Singapore containing files on every operative her old agency ever burned—including herself. The leak traces back to someone inside her own crew, and as the magnate's rivals close in, Xanthe realizes the only way out is to sell the server's location to the highest bidder before a dawn extraction flight. But the buyer she chooses turns out to be the handler who erased her identity years ago, forcing her to choose between reclaiming her old name and protecting the makeshift family her crew has become. In the end, she burns the server instead, trades her silence for her team's freedom, and boards the flight alone—finally invisible by choice rather than by force.
about_author: Lena Ravensworth is the pen name of a former maritime insurance investigator who spent a decade documenting the gray economies of Mediterranean ports. She writes thrillers about people whose loyalties are bought, sold, and occasionally given for free.

chapters.title: Salt and Contracts
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. On assignment guarding shipping magnate Étienne Vasseur at Marseille's old port, Xanthe runs a routine biometric sweep of new staff. A stray voiceprint from a dockworker's radio pings something buried in her encrypted kit—a partial match to her own scrubbed voice signature. Beat: unease beneath professional calm; the past stirring.

chapters.title: The Client Nobody Trusts
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Vasseur reveals he's expecting an audit from partners he clearly fears, and asks Xanthe to quietly identify leaks among his staff. Her crew—fixer Marisol, tech Osei, driver Tomas—debate whether to take the off-books job. Beat: found-family warmth tested by money and mistrust; Xanthe hides what the voiceprint told her.

chapters.title: Voiceprint
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Following the audio thread through relay servers, she reaches a node in Singapore that unlocks against her voice alone: a dossier labeled with a name she hasn't used in seven years. Inside are files on dozens of erased operatives—and a live counter showing someone else accessing it right now. Beat: vertigo; identity as a weapon pointed at her.

chapters.title: Everyone Is Lying Beautifully
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Xanthe and Marisol. Marisol, running her own quiet investigation into Vasseur's audit, notices Xanthe's midnight work sessions and suspects betrayal. Meanwhile Vasseur's rival, the Callas syndicate, makes Xanthe an offer for anything she learns. Beat: paranoia spreading through the crew like damp through plaster.

chapters.title: The Handler's Hand
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Tracing the concurrent access, she finds a familiar operational fingerprint: Wren, the handler who once erased her identity and vanished. A dead-drop message arrives—Wren knows she's found the server and offers a meeting in exchange for 'the thing you took.' Beat: dread mixed with a shameful flicker of longing for the person who made her invisible.

chapters.title: Blood on the Quay
chapters.summary: POV: Tomas. A Callas hit team mistakes Tomas for Xanthe's courier and puts him in the hospital. The crew closes ranks; Marisol confronts Xanthe, demanding the truth. Xanthe finally shows them the dossier—their names could be in it too. Beat: rupture and repair; loyalty chosen explicitly rather than assumed.

chapters.title: Auction at Dawn Minus Two
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. With 48 hours until the extraction flight, Xanthe opens bidding: Callas wants the server, Vasseur wants leverage over his partners, and Wren wants it destroyed—or so they claim. She realizes whoever wins will also own everyone named inside. Beat: cold clarity; power revealed as a market where she is both seller and stock.

chapters.title: The Meeting at Fort Saint-Jean
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Wren appears in person—older, softer, still dangerous—and admits the server was bait to flush out surviving operatives before a corporate purge. They offer Xanthe her old name back if she hands over access. Beat: the climax of temptation; identity offered back like a leash disguised as a gift.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Xanthe and Osei. Instead of selling, Xanthe and Osei trigger a cascading wipe of the server hours before the flight, while Marisol stalls Callas enforcers and Vasseur's own audit explodes into open war on the docks. Beat: chaos as catharsis; the crew fighting as one unit for the first time.

chapters.title: The Last Flight Out
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. At dawn, with Callas closing in and Wren watching from the terminal crowd, Xanthe boards the extraction flight carrying nothing but her crew's new identities—forged clean, untraceable. She leaves her old name burning behind her and, for the first time, chooses who she'll be tomorrow. Beat: bittersweet resolution; invisibility reclaimed as freedom, not erasure.
